content: Acyclovir may also help reduce the duration of pain that persists after the sores have healed. How to Use: Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. Typically, it is taken 2 to 5 times a day. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, ensure you shake the bottle well before each dose. Use a special measuring device or spoon to carefully measure the prescribed dose. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not provide an accurate measurement. This medication is most effective when started at the first sign of an outbreak, as instructed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body by taking it at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, headache, or vomiting. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Precautions: Before taking acyclovir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, valacyclovir, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Acyclovir does not prevent the spread of genital herpes. To reduce the risk of transmitting herpes to your partner, avoid sexual contact during an outbreak or if you have symptoms. It is possible to spread genital herpes even if you do not have symptoms. Always use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activity. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Acyclovir passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Acyclovir is very similar to valacyclovir. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
